en: The Jātaka:
The Ninth Chapter, The Section on Vultures (Gijjhavagga)
7. The Lomasakassapa Jātaka:
“O King, may you be like Indra, forever free from aging and death.”
“If you were to perform a sacrifice,
[you should sacrifice] the seer Lomasakassapa.
“The one who encompasses the entire ocean...”
One would not desire even the earth girt by the oceans along with its censure;
know this, O Seyya, to be so.
Fie on that gain of fame and gain of wealth,
O brahmin, which is a livelihood through falling into ruin!
Or by practicing unrighteousness.
Yet even if one goes forth as a homeless wanderer, taking up the alms-bowl;
That very livelihood is better than seeking it through unrighteousness,
even if one were to take up a bowl.
Let one wander as a homeless renunciant;
even a kingdom is better than that which involves harm toward others in this world.
“Power belongs to the moon, power to the sun,
power to ascetics and brahmins;
power belongs to the ocean’s shoreline.”
Women possess great power and exceeding strength,
just as they did with the seer Lomasakassapa when he was practicing intense austerities.
For the sake of her father,
Candavatī performed the Vājapeyya sacrifice.
That deed, committed out of greed—
Bitterness has sensual desire as its cause;
I shall seek out its root and cut off passion along with all its bonds.
Fie on the many sensual pleasures in this world!
Asceticism, O King, is far superior to the strands of sensual pleasure.
Having abandoned sensual pleasures, I shall practice asceticism.
“May your kingdom alone be possessed of the Candavatī [pearl]!
Thus ends the seventh Jātaka, the Lomasakassapa Jātaka.
